identity.title: Linearly polarized millimeter and submillimeter continuum emission of Sgr A* constrained by ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report continuum emission properties of Sgr A* at the above frequency bands, based on the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) observations.

question.value: What are the polarized continuum properties (Stokes I, polarization position angle, polarization percentage) of Sgr A* at ~100, 230, 345, 500 and 700 GHz?

evidence.quote: Our aim is to characterize the polarized continuum emission properties including intensity, polarization position angle, and polarization percentage of Sgr A*

method.value: CASA calibration, uvcontsub, exportfits, convert to Miriad

evidence.quote: Finally, we used the Miriad 4.3.8 (Sault et al. 1995) task `fits` to convert the fits format data into the Miriad data format

analysis_steps.goal: Measure XX and YY point-source fluxes vs parallactic angle

method.value: Modified Miriad uvamp fitting a point source per 5 deg parallactic-angle bin; band 3 uv>30 klambda

evidence.quote: We fit the fluxes of the XX and the YY correlations separately for every 5$^{\circ}$ bin of parallactic angle.

assumptions.value: Source spatially compact so missing short spacings not a concern

evidence.quote: the emission source of our interest is spatially very compact (Bower et al. 2014)

method.value: Sinusoidal fit of (XX-YY)/2I - delta = P cos(2(Psi - eta - phi)) with bootstrap-like perturbation

evidence.quote: P, $\Psi$, and $\delta$ and their errors are determined by mean and standard deviations of fittings to 1000 independent realizations

key_parameters.value: 1000 realizations, Gaussian noise sigma^Q from prior-fit residuals

evidence.quote: we disturb each data point of $(XX- YY)/2I$ with a Gaussian random number of which the standard deviation is $\sigma^Q$

assumptions.value: P and Psi constant during each track

evidence.quote: If the polarization position angle and the polarization percentage do not vary significantly in a shorter timescale than the durations of our observing tracks

fitting.value: Least-squares sinusoid fit with Q offset delta free

evidence.loc: Polarization fitting, intrinsic polarization angle, and rotation measure
evidence.quote: we perform a prior fitting of $P$, $\delta$ and $\Psi$, based on XX and YY observed at various $\eta$.

validation.value: Means checked to converge to prior fits; calibrators fitted

evidence.quote: We have checked that those means converged to the values close to a priori fittings.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit intrinsic angle and rotation measure

method.value: Least squares fit of chi0 and RM to band 3, 6, 7 angles

evidence.quote: Least square fitting of the band 3, 6 and 7 observations on 2012 May 18 yield $\chi_{0}$=138$^{\circ}$$\pm$6$^{\circ}$

assumptions.value: Constant chi0 and RM; different photospheres ignored

evidence.quote: our analysis here does not consider the effect that the observations at different frequencies may trace the different photospheres
were carried out using the CASA software package (McMullin et al. 2007) version 4.5

used_for.value: Data conversion and flux measurement (modified uvamp)

evidence.quote: We modified the Miriad task `uvamp`, to permit fitting fluxes for a point source as a function of the parallactic angle

findings_qualitative.value: Polarized emission detected in all bands; P increases monotonically with frequency below 500 GHz

evidence.quote: Below 500 GHz, we see a monotonic increase of polarization percentage with frequency.

claims.hypothesis: Is emission at >500 GHz optically thin?
claims.experiment: Compare Stokes I at ~490 and ~690 GHz
claims.finding: Emission at >~500 GHz may be optically thin

evidence.quote: The $\sim$690 GHz observations on 2015 May 02 shows lower Stokes I flux than that of the $\sim$490 GHz observations taken on 2015 April 30.

claims.experiment: Fit chi0 and RM from 2012 data and compare with earlier work
claims.finding: Intrinsic angle likely varies with time

evidence.quote: The fitted $\chi_{0}$ from the 2012 May 18 observations deviates significantly from those of the earlier observations.

limitations_admitted.value: Band 9 parallactic angle coverage limited, so P may be overestimated; no polarization calibration

evidence.quote: A better constraint on $P$ requires future observations which incorporate polarization calibration, or cover sufficiently large parallactic angle ranges.

reproducibility.score_reason: Public archival data and clear fit formula, but custom code and calibration details missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Custom modified Miriad task and deferred calibration details prevent a complete recipe.
